articles.title: Strategy for a Software Developer in Egypt to Transition from Unpaid Family Labor to Financial Independence Through Coding
articles.excerpt: Systemic Architecture Analysis At a critical juncture marked by the milestone of age 30, the subject operates within a tightly coupled socio-economic feedback loop combining centralized household fina…
articles.body: Systemic Architecture Analysis At a critical juncture marked by the milestone of age 30, the subject operates within a tightly coupled socio-economic feedback loop combining centralized household finances, unpaid enterprise labor, and interrupted technical skill acquisition. This structural configuration creates severe systemic friction, threatening long-term autonomy and career viability unless rigorously dismantled. Resource Lock: Labor output from the family factory generates revenue that is entirely captured by the household head, preventing the accumulation of liquid capital. This lack of personal capital creates an economic dependency trap, eliminating the ability to independently acquire necessary hardware upgrades or transition time toward career pivots.
articles.author: Ilya Selivanov

articles.excerpt: For a long time our sitemap at RAMO was one big file. Every product, every category, every article, the contact page, the shipping policy, all in one list. It validated, Google read it, and nobody tho…
articles.body: For a long time our sitemap at RAMO was one big file. Every product, every category, every article, the contact page, the shipping policy, all in one list. It validated, Google read it, and nobody thought about it again. The problem showed up later, in Search Console. When the indexing report said "Discovered, currently not indexed" for a pile of URLs, I had no fast way to tell what kind of pages they were. Product pages? Old article URLs? Brand pages nobody links to? With one sitemap you get one bucket of numbers, and one bucket doesn't tell you where to look. So we split it.
articles.author: RAMO

articles.title: Black code text survived CRF 33 in a lecture recording, red text was soft at CRF 18
articles.excerpt: The question I wanted answered about lecture-style screen recordings: how high can CRF go before slide text gets hard to read? The usual rule is that lower CRF means better quality, which doesn't say…
articles.body: The question I wanted answered about lecture-style screen recordings: how high can CRF go before slide text gets hard to read? The usual rule is that lower CRF means better quality, which doesn't say whether a line of code survives when the goal is a smaller file. So I ran a CRF ladder on one recording and measured the text directly. Black code text barely moved until CRF 33 and only dropped clearly at 43. Red text on the same frame was already soft at CRF 18, and that turned out to have little to do with CRF. The recording is not a real class. It's a 4-minute mock lecture recording I built myself (slides flipping, mouse, typing, a scrolling handout), 1920×1080, 30 fps, encoded at a constant 12 Mbps that I picked as an assumption (not any recorder's default), 360.0 MB, no audio.
articles.author: yue xing

articles.title: What I learned building an AI tool to remove people from photos
articles.excerpt: I'm a solo developer, and my second side project is a small web tool that lets you remove a person from a photo: you paint over a photobomber, tap Remove, and the AI fills the area with background. It…
articles.body: I'm a solo developer, and my second side project is a small web tool that lets you remove a person from a photo : you paint over a photobomber, tap Remove, and the AI fills the area with background. It sounds like a solved problem. It mostly is, until someone uploads a photo from a restaurant. Version 1: LaMa, and why it is so good on beaches The first version uses LaMa , the classic inpainting model. You send an image and a black-and-white mask (white = remove), and it fills the hole using what it sees around it. On Replicate it runs in about 1.4 seconds and costs about $0.0003 per image, which is cheap enough to offer three free removals a day without thinking twice.

articles.title: H.265 isn't what makes screen recordings small
articles.excerpt: If you ship a small product, you send screen recordings all the time: a demo for a client, a walkthrough, a bug repro. The file a recorder hands you can be far bigger than four minutes of slides shoul…
articles.body: If you ship a small product, you send screen recordings all the time: a demo for a client, a walkthrough, a bug repro. The file a recorder hands you can be far bigger than four minutes of slides should be, and a common reflex is to export it again as H.265, the newer codec most export dialogs now list. On the test clip below, that switch was worth 3%. What decided the size was how the encoder spends bits on frames that don't change, and how often it forces a keyframe. The numbers come from one synthetic clip, not a real session. It imitates a 4-minute lecture-style recording, built from screenshots of a hand-written page: page turns, a cursor, typing, a notes panel that scrolls.
articles.author: AsyncMonk

articles.title: Ping64|Inside a Cable Factory Where One Misplaced Spec Sheet Could Delay an Entire Certification Cycle
articles.excerpt: In a mid-sized cable plant, a production supervisor spent Friday evening looking for the insulation specification attached to a medium-voltage order scheduled to restart on Monday morning. Two revisio…
articles.body: In a mid-sized cable plant, a production supervisor spent Friday evening looking for the insulation specification attached to a medium-voltage order scheduled to restart on Monday morning. Two revisions of the same spec sheet sat on the shared drive, one saved by an engineer months earlier and one attached to a long email thread. The QC team could not confirm which version reflected the latest standards update, so the batch was placed on hold. By Sunday night the supervisor had asked three departments, checked two personal folders, and still had no authoritative answer. Nobody wanted to restart a line against a specification that might have been superseded. Hold periods like this rarely appear in production reports, yet they may cost several days.

articles.excerpt: Prime Video's LOTR prequel series remains infuriatingly inconsistent
articles.body: There are several scenes in Rings of Power season 3 that have direct parallels to key moments in Jackson’s films. The elves Galadriel (Morfydd Clark) and Arondir (Ismael Cruz Córdova) travel into enemy territory with an unreliable guide who doesn’t like elf food and pits the friends against each other, just like Gollum does with Frodo and Sam. Galadriel finds herself hiding in a hedge from a Nazgnagôl, the still-living precursors to the Ringwraiths that would put Frodo and his Hobbit friends in the exact same position. At one point, Galadriel evokes the power of “fellowship” as something that can provide hope against Sauron, and it feels almost as hamfisted as Elrond name-dropping the title of The Fellowship of the Ring in Rivendell.
